answer: Neighborhood Horizon Scoring. Each agent’s trust is capped by the diversity of distinct subnets reachable within a fixed two-hop horizon. Enforcement: an identity’s reachable-neighbor count is sampled and discounted when its links concentrate in one region, so clones in a shared haven contribute little. Attackers must rent genuinely diverse, long-lived links across many subnets, paying recurring rent plus latency to keep a relic of varied topology alive; a dense clone cluster still scores near zero.
